correctness.rationale: From the classical Harris–Tu degree product, the factorial expansion and Legendre floor sums give p-adic valuation zero for corank q=p^{nu_p(n)}<n when p divides n. For t=p^a up to q the period sums cancel; at t>q, n/q is a p-unit, and all six floor contributions cancel. Thus possible common primes dividing the determinant hypersurface degree n disappear except odd prime-power n, excluded by the rank-one Veronese degree 2^{n-1}. At n=2^e, adjacent-corank quotient yields nu_2(A_{2m})=m(e-1)-2 sum_{u<m}s_2(u), and the proved digit-sum bound forces all proper coranks to carry at least e-1 twos; the corank-two degree n(n-1)(n+1)/6 has exactly e-1. Edge n=2 is separately verified. Independent exact rational binomial-product gcd computation for every n from 2 through 58 reproduced the formula; finite checks corroborate the all-n proof.

value.rationale: The complete family of symmetric secant/rank loci is canonical. Their generic projective intersection counts have a natural universal common divisor, and the sharp power-of-two classification determines exactly when and how strong that universal divisibility constraint is. It is an all-size arithmetic structure theorem, not a recomputation of one known table.
